advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pre-assert the `rm -rf` and `git clone` substrings exist in the body before calling `body.index()` so a removed line yields a clear assertion failure rather than a ValueError.
evidence: tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:439: `clone_at = body.index("git clone --single-branch --branch tickets")`
tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:440: `rm_at = body.index('rm -rf "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"')`
Only `rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` is guarded by an `assert ... in body`; the `rm`/`clone` substrings are not pre-checked, so their absence surfaces as ValueError rather than a failed assertion.
advisory.finding: The test asserts presence of the `rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` guard but reaches for `rm -rf ...` and `git clone ...` via `body.index(...)`, which raises an uninformative ValueError (not a clear assertion message) if either line were removed or renamed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Serialize the re-clone (e.g. `flock` on a lockfile in ${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}) so two containers sharing the persistent volume cannot interleave `rm -rf`/`git clone` into the same directory.
evidence: Shared mutable resource: the persistent tickets volume `${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}` — commit msg: 'the named volume persists across containers' and comment line 107 'every later container inherited the poisoned volume'
≥2 executors: blue-green deploy repeatedly spawns containers over the same volume (comment line 104 'the 120s health rollback did, repeatedly'); each runs `provision_store &` at Dockerfile.mcp:123

Interleaving window: WRITE `rm -rf "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"/.[!.]* "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"/*` (line 112) then WRITE `git clone ... "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"` (line 113) with no flock/lock; the detecting gate `if ! git ... rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` (line 109) does not exclude a second container

Harm: two concurrent clones/rm into one directory corrupt the fresh store (partial objects deleted / clone-into-non-empty) — same poisoned store the change set out to prevent, produced by racing self-heal
Guard disposition: rev-parse DETECTS unusability then proceeds to clear+clone anyway; it does not serialize, so it is not a suppressing guard
Shared mutable resource: contents of `${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}` read by every MCP read via `_tracker` (src/rebar/_reads.py:41-51)
≥2 executors: `provision_store &` (Dockerfile.mcp:123) backgrounded, then `exec "$@"` (Dockerfile.mcp:124) launches the reading server — both run at once

Interleaving window: WRITE `rm -rf "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"/.[!.]* "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"/*` (line 112) removes contents but leaves the dir; READ `if not os.path.isdir(tracker)` (src/rebar/_reads.py:42) sees the dir present so does NOT raise store_uninitialized, reads proceed and return `[]`

Harm: during the window the server answers `[]` (silent-empty) instead of the honest `store_uninitialized` — the exact failure mode the read guard was built to eliminate, now triggered by clearing a store under a live reader
advisory.finding: The new `rm -rf` + `git clone` re-clone sequence added to provision_store is unserialized across containers that share the persistent named volume: two containers can each read HEAD as unresolvable, pass the rev-parse gate, and interleave `rm -rf`/`git clone` into the same directory, corrupting the store (one clone's objects deleted by the other's rm, or clone writing into a half-cleared tree).
merged_from: The added `rm -rf` empties the existing tracker directory in place while the server (started via `exec "$@"` concurrently with the backgrounded provisioner) serves reads; because the directory itself persists, `_tracker` returns `[]` rather than `store_uninitialized` for the rm→clone window, re-exposing the silent-empty failure to live readers.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the destructive `rm -rf` with a non-empty assertion, e.g. `: "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR:?}"` before deleting.
evidence: infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:112: echo '      rm -rf "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"/.[!.]* "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"/* 2>/dev/null || true';
infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:81: ENV REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets (default present, but nothing re-asserts non-empty at the rm site)
ABSENCE: no `[ -n "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}" ]` / `${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR:?}` assertion before the destructive rm
infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:109: echo '    if ! git -C "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}" rev-parse --verify -q HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then';
infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:42: COPY . /app (so /app, the WORKDIR, is itself a git working tree)
infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:33: WORKDIR /app
advisory.finding: The re-clone clears the persistent tracker volume with `rm -rf "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"/.[!.]* "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"/*` with no guard that REBAR_TRACKER_DIR is non-empty; a future refactor that unsets/blanks the var expands this to `rm -rf /.[!.]* /*`, a full container-root wipe.
merged_from: The HEAD guard runs `git -C "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}" rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`; if REBAR_TRACKER_DIR is empty/unset, `git -C ""` resolves against the CWD /app (itself a git repo cloned at COPY . /app), so HEAD resolves, the guard mis-fires as 'usable', and the clone is silently skipped against the wrong path.
scenarios: A later change makes REBAR_TRACKER_DIR overridable at runtime and it is passed empty
advisory.suggested_fix: Prefix the clear with a required-var assertion: `echo '      : "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR:?tracker dir must be set}"';` (or wrap the rm in `[ -n "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}" ] && rm -rf ...`).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the substring/ordering grep with an execution test that drives the entrypoint shell against a poisoned-store fixture.
evidence: tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:433: `assert "rev-parse --verify -q HEAD" in body`
tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:438-441: `guard_at = body.index("rev-parse --verify -q HEAD")` ... `assert guard_at < rm_at < clone_at`

The unit under test is the generated shell entrypoint inside Dockerfile.mcp (the changed behavior), so grepping its literal command tokens tests implementation text, not behavior — Rule-5's instruction-artifact exception does not apply to executable source under test.
advisory.finding: The new test asserts the literal command tokens (`rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`, `rm -rf`) and their ordering in the Dockerfile source rather than executing the entrypoint, making it a change-detector/source-grep over the implementation text: a behavior-preserving refactor of the guard (equivalent HEAD-resolvability check via `git symbolic-ref`/`git cat-file`, or reordering) breaks it with no observable-behavior change.
scenarios: A future maintainer swaps `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` for an equivalent HEAD-resolvability probe; the store still self-heals identically but the test fails.
The guard is refactored/reordered while preserving semantics; the ordering assertion breaks.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an execution test: run the generated entrypoint (or the guard fragment) against a fixture with a dangling HEAD and assert the store is cleared and re-cloned, and against a healthy store assert HEAD-preservation (no re-clone).
evidence: The diff adds the re-clone shell logic as new (`+`) lines in infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp (the `if ! git -C ... rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` guard, the `rm -rf` clear, and the branch to `git clone`).
tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:430-441: the only new test reads `_DOCKERFILE.read_text(...)` and asserts substring presence + `body.index` ordering; it never runs the script.
search of tests/ for `provision_store` returns only the text-assertion tests in test_mcp_on_box_infra.py — no execution harness exercises the entrypoint's clone/re-clone guard (absence rationale).
An execution harness pattern exists: tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py runs shell with git stubs and asserts on resulting git state, so driving this shell is feasible.
blocking.finding: No test drives the actual re-clone behavior: the poisoned-store (unresolvable HEAD) -> clear-and-re-clone path and the healthy-store -> skip path are never executed. Named violating inputs the current substring/order assertions cannot catch: (1) a guard emitted without `-C "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"` so it probes the wrong directory; (2) the `rm -rf "${REBAR_TRACKER_DIR}"/.[!.]* ...` glob failing to remove the `.git` directory (dotfile-glob semantics vary by /bin/sh) so the partial store survives into the retry. Both leave the substring and ordering assertions green.
scenarios: The `rm -rf` glob silently leaves `.git`, so re-clone into a non-empty dir fails and the poisoned store persists — commit's central claim regresses undetected.
The `rev-parse` guard loses its `-C` scope and always resolves the container CWD's HEAD, so a poisoned store is never re-cloned — undetected.
